title: Public rebuilding operations expose conversion from wildfire damage into permits and construction stages, while household recovery remains unobserved
source_unit: Los Angeles County 2025 Fire Rebuilding Power BI public dashboard; model schema, aggregate measures, and construction-stage query results
geography: Los Angeles County fire-rebuilding dashboard; default public dashboard scope, with unincorporated damaged/destroyed measures and fire-area filters where exposed

observations.period: Model refreshed September 29, 2026 at 21:27:25 UTC; queried September 30, 2026 UTC

model_entities.value: Fire Area; Parcels and Units; Applications, Permits and Zoning Review Count; Permit Turnaround; Construction Stages; Applications, Issuance and Completions

observations.method: Retrieved the public Power BI semantic-model schema and models/exploration metadata, then queried the published aggregate visuals through the public querydata endpoint. No address, permit number, or respondent-level field was extracted into this record.
observations.uncertainty: The dashboard's refresh time, default filters, revision history, geographic scope, and measure definitions control interpretation. A model refresh is not proof that every underlying property has current status or that categories are mutually exclusive.
observations.subgroup: Public dashboard model and its published administrative measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: A rich public operational dashboard can improve visibility without creating a longitudinal household panel; its counts can reflect workflow status rather than completed recovery.

observations.period: Dashboard refresh September 29, 2026; default aggregate card

denominator.unit: unincorporated damaged/destroyed-unit estimate in the public dashboard

observations.method: Power BI aggregate card measures named Damaged/Destroyed Properties (UA) and Damaged/Destroyed Parcels (UA).
observations.uncertainty: These are dashboard estimates and do not establish unique households, insurance status, claim filing, loss severity, displacement duration, or rebuild eligibility.
observations.subgroup: Unincorporated-area properties and units within the dashboard's published damage universe.
observations.counterinterpretation: Units and parcels are not interchangeable: multi-unit properties, accessory structures, and property classification can make counts diverge without implying different household experiences.

denominator.unit: records across published construction stages for Eaton and Palisades dashboard scope

observations.method: Power BI Construction Stages table query with the published non-null stage filter; the displayed stage counts sum to 1,752.
observations.uncertainty: A stage record is not necessarily a unique property or household, and a finaled/ready stage is not proof of occupancy, affordability, insurance payment, or safe return.
observations.subgroup: Published construction-stage records in the dashboard scope.
observations.counterinterpretation: The stage distribution may represent the current visible workflow rather than all damaged properties; unobserved repairs, private rebuilding, delayed permits, and properties outside the dashboard can be substantial.

observations.period: Dashboard refresh September 29, 2026; permit-type stage cards
observations.method: Power BI permit-type measure queries for published issued/in-construction/completed strings.
observations.uncertainty: The cards are measure outputs, not a common-denominator property ledger. The record does not infer completion rates by dividing categories because issued, construction, and completed measures may have distinct universes and timing.
observations.subgroup: Published permit categories in the dashboard scope.
observations.counterinterpretation: A low completed count may reflect construction timing, inspection scheduling, reporting lag, or category definitions rather than failed recovery.

observations.period: Dashboard refresh September 29, 2026; administrative throughput and waiting measures

denominator.unit: published dashboard throughput and turnaround measure set

observations.method: Power BI category visual 943427878 and turnaround visuals 943427819, 943427851, 943427832, and 943427881; aggregate published measure queries only, with no address or permit-level rows extracted.
observations.uncertainty: These categories and stages have distinct universes and timing. The counts cannot be chained as a funnel or used to calculate a completion rate. The waiting measures describe administrative workflow time, not household time burden or displacement duration.
observations.subgroup: Published dashboard scope; fire-area filters and default scope must be preserved when reproducing the measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher cleared, issued, or completed counts can coexist with unequal access, insurance or payment delays, contractor scarcity, and continued household displacement.

observations.period: June 8, 2026; Los Angeles County DEO/LAEDC third economic update on the Eaton and Palisades wildfire recovery

denominator.unit: official county recovery update using rebuilding, occupancy, mobility, labor, vacancy, and local-spending indicators

metro_ridership_change.unit: percent versus adjusted pre-fire baseline, first quarter 2026

annual_localized_spending_loss_palisades.unit: US dollars estimated annual local spending loss

annual_localized_spending_loss_eaton.unit: US dollars estimated annual local spending loss

observations.method: Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity and LAEDC economic update combining USPS vacancy, rebuilding permit and certificate-of-occupancy data, employment and job-posting data, transit ridership, and localized spending and service indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The update combines indicators with different denominators, dates, and geographic coverage. Its destroyed-structure and survivor shares are not a linked household panel; the source does not identify insurance payment adequacy, claim status, temporary housing by person, mortgage continuity, or whether a completed/occupancy-approved structure is occupied by the pre-fire household.
observations.subgroup: Eaton and Palisades fire-impacted communities in Los Angeles County; measures include destroyed structures, survivors, local transit, and fire-area economic indicators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Permit issuance and occupancy approval may reflect meaningful administrative progress, while the very low completion share and assistance exhaustion signal may reflect construction timing, insurance and financing constraints, contractor capacity, or measurement lag; the update alone cannot identify the binding mechanism for each household.

related_sources.claim: LA County describes the wildfire impact dashboard as covering housing/displacement, workers/businesses, communities, and environmental conditions.
California DOI provides a separate aggregate claims and payment surface for the Eaton and Palisades fires.

Los Angeles County DEO and LAEDC report rebuilding permits, occupancy approval, displacement-assistance exhaustion, transit, local spending, and labor-market indicators for the Eaton and Palisades recovery.

boundary: This record adds a public administrative and multi-indicator recovery layer from damage estimates through permits, construction stages, occupancy approval, displacement-assistance pressure, mobility, and local economic function. It does not establish insurance payment, claim adequacy, repair completion at a named property, occupancy by the original household, temporary housing, mortgage continuity, household mobility, or durable recovery. Address and permit-number fields are present in the public schema but were intentionally not extracted here; county economic-update indicators remain separate denominators.

reproduction_audit.extraction_scope: Aggregate visual queries plus one official county economic-update observation; no address-level, permit-number, or respondent-level output
reproduction_audit.status: reproduced from public Power BI schema and querydata endpoint
